Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection, reporting pain and reduced motion in the right shoulder.
The mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported force and direction of the crash, and the clinical picture fits an acute
soft-tissue and rotator cuff strain. Over eight visits, care included physical examination, range-of-motion testing, targeted
therapeutic exercise, and home exercise instruction. Several examination findings, including limited abduction and tenderness
over the supraspinatus, support the reported injury, while neurological screening and strength testing within the normal limits
were unremarkable. The patient's history includes treatment to the same shoulder region within the past two years, and that prior
condition is likely contributing to some of the current symptoms. Treatment followed a typical course, with visit frequency
decreasing as the patient improved and symptoms became more manageable. Billing records reflect single, non-duplicated
charges for each service rendered. Ongoing home exercise and follow-up as needed are recommended.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
